motion: Does the evidence from cosmology, fine-tuning, morality, Jesus' resurrection, and religious experience make Christian theism more reasonable than skeptical atheism?

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning, Causation, and a Personal Creator
sections.rationale: This opening section follows the earliest exchange from the universe's beginning and causal explanation through the proposed attributes and personality of its cause, including the later scientific, causal, and infinity-focused replies. Its weight reflects the number and structural depth of the linked cosmological steps.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive chain from a finite beginning to a transcendent cause and its proposed nonphysical attributes.
This supplies the separate load-bearing step from a nonphysical cause to an unembodied mind and personal creator.
This is a principal challenge to extending ordinary causal experience from material rearrangement to creation from nothing.
This major scientific reply addresses whether current cosmology establishes an absolute beginning rather than merely a beginning of expansion.
This major reply addresses the distinct inference from a nonphysical cause to a substrate-independent mind.
This major counter-reply returns to the cosmological evidence and the claimed scope of the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin theorem.
This major counter-reply develops the causal-principle exchange concerning efficient and material causes.
This major reply addresses the philosophical argument against an actual infinite through the arithmetic of infinite collections.
This major counter-reply completes the selected exchange about infinite subtraction and physically instantiated collections.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Alternative Explanations, and Designer Specificity
sections.rationale: This section begins with the fine-tuning constructive and follows the exchange over cosmic probabilities, deeper physics, multiverse alternatives, and what properties a designer inference could establish. The weight represents a distinct evidential line with several independent structural questions.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive comparison among physical necessity, chance, and design.
This concession marks supporting common ground about when fine-tuning would invite a designer explanation.
This is a principal multi-part reply concerning probability, deeper physical explanation, and multiverse scenarios.
This major reply raises the separate specificity issue of whether fine-tuning identifies a morally perfect Christian God.
This major counter-reply addresses both parameter-range probabilities and the cumulative role of separate evidential arguments.
This concession clarifies the limited divine attribute attributed to the selected evidential arguments.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Divine Character, and the Evidence of Evil
sections.rationale: This section starts with the moral constructive, then groups the exchange over whether objective value requires God, how naturalism might ground value and obligation, and whether evil fits a perfect deity. Its weight reflects the interaction between a positive moral line and a distinct contrary-evidence line.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive route from objective moral values to a divine ground.
This major reply separates apprehension of objective value and intrinsic human worth from belief in God.
This major counter-reply develops the questions of nonarbitrary value and binding moral obligation under naturalism.
This is the load-bearing contrary-evidence move connecting observed evil and purported divine morality to expectations about a perfect God.
This major reply supplies a proposed purpose-based explanation for permitting natural and moral evil.

sections.title: Resurrection Evidence and Historical Sources
sections.rationale: This section isolates the resurrection line because it turns on a distinctive historical record: the empty tomb, appearances, disciples' belief, source dependence, discrepancies, and historian agreement. Its weight reflects an independent route to specifically Christian theism with a compact direct exchange.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive inference from three claimed historical facts to resurrection.
This major reply addresses dating, authorship, source dependence, and discrepancies in the Gospel evidence.
This major counter-reply focuses the historical exchange on scholarly acceptance of the three selected facts.

sections.title: Religious Experience, Rival Hypotheses, and the Cumulative Burden
sections.rationale: This final section begins with personal religious experience and follows the chronological exchange over religious disagreement, competing hypotheses, the required comparative case, and absence-of-evidence reasoning. Its weight reflects its role in connecting one evidential line to the debate's cumulative and motion-level framing.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the load-bearing constructive presentation of immediate personal experience as an independent way of knowing God.
This major reply uses conflicting religious outcomes to question the reliability of shared belief-forming sources.
This load-bearing constructive sets the comparative burden among the specific Christian claim and numerous rival hypotheses.
This major counter-reply disputes the claim of one common religious method and restates the combined evidential method.
This major counter-reply addresses the expectation needed for absence of evidence to count against God's existence.

bridgeMappings.rationale: The motion-level route is retained through its five constructive evidential lines, each assigned to the chronological topical section devoted to that line and its exchange.
The cumulative convergence bridge is represented across all five sections by the principal constructive lines and later moves connecting those lines to rival hypotheses and contrary evidence.
The finite-beginning and transcendent-cause bridge is concentrated in section-01 through its constructive causal steps and retained replies about cosmology, causation, and actual infinity.
The design-from-fine-tuning bridge is retained in section-02 through the initial necessity-chance-design comparison and the later defense of probability and multiple fine-tuning cases.
The resurrection bridge is retained in section-04 through the three-fact constructive inference and the later historical reply concerning scholarly acceptance of those facts.
The contrary motion-level route is retained through the comparative rival-hypothesis framework in section-05 and the empirical argument from evil and divine character in section-03.
The central skeptical route spans all five sections through retained challenges to causal, fine-tuning, moral, resurrection, experiential, and specifically Christian inferences.
The skeptical Kalam bridge is concentrated in section-01 through the retained challenges concerning creation from nothing, an absolute beginning, an unembodied mind, and actual infinity.
The skeptical fine-tuning bridge is retained in section-02 through the conditional concession, probability and alternative-explanation cautions, and designer-specificity challenge.
The contrary-evidence bridge from evil and opaque divine presence is retained in section-03 through the move comparing the observed world and purported divine morality with a perfect God.
